claims.source: Analysis of the distribution of these subpopulations in the different datasets (Figure 1D) confirmed the presence of five mesenchyme subpopulations previously identified in cycling mouse uterine tissue (V, P1, F1-3; Kirkwood et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: Supported by comparison to previous scRNAseq data from Kirkwood et al., 2021 and shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Three additional transcriptionally distinct repair-specific cell clusters were identified: P2 and F4 in 24 hr tissues and F5 in 48 hr tissues.
claims.source: However in tissue recovered at 24 and 48 hr three additional transcriptionally distinct repair-specific cell clusters were identified: P2 and F4 in 24 hr tissues (Figure 1D; green and purple circles respectively) and F5 present in 48 hr tissues (Figure 1D; pink ellipse).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data and visualization in Figure 1D showing clusters specific to repair timepoints.

claims.claim: P2 showed a very high degree of similarity to P1 (previously identified as pericytes).
claims.source: Differential gene expression analysis revealed a very high degree of similarity between P1 (previously identified as pericytes) (Kirkwood et al., 2021) and P2 which was specific to 24 hr tissue (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: Based on differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Unbiased GO analysis of the P2 transcriptome identified functions associated with blood vessel formation and immune cell signalling, characteristic of pericytes.
claims.source: Unbiased GO analysis of the P2 transcriptome identified functions associated with blood vessel formation and immune cell signalling, characteristic of pericytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D(i)) suggesting a role for these cells in angiogenesis and regulation of the immune system in response to changes in the local environment.
claims.evidence: Based on gene ontology analysis of P2 cluster shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D(i).

claims.claim: Cluster F5 expressed a large number of mitochondrial genes and genes associated with cell death including Casp3, Casp9, Trp53 and Bax.
claims.source: We noted that cluster F5 (specific to 48 hr tissue) expressed a large number of mitochondrial genes and genes associated with cell death including Casp3, Casp9, Trp53 and Bax (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: GO analysis of the F5 transcriptome identified functions associated with DNA damage.
claims.source: GO analysis of the F5 transcriptome identified functions associated with DNA damage.
claims.evidence: Based on gene ontology analysis of F5 cluster transcriptome.

claims.claim: F5 represents a cluster of dead/apoptotic cells.
claims.source: Based on this in silico data and the results in our previous study using the same mouse model system that detected high levels of cleaved caspase expression in the stromal compartment at 24 hr (Armstrong et al., 2017) we suggest that F5 represents a cluster of dead/apoptotic cells and it was therefore excluded from further downstream analyses.
claims.evidence: Based on scRNAseq data showing apoptosis markers and previous experimental data from Armstrong et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Cluster F4 had a transcriptomic signature that was distinct from mesenchymal cell populations (F1-3) present in cycling endometrium.
claims.source: Cluster F4 (24 hr tissue) was of particular interest as it had a transcriptomic signature that was distinct from to those of the mesenchymal cell populations (F1-3) present in cycling endometrium (Kirkwood et al., 2021; Figure 2A; red box).
claims.evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Unbiased GO analysis of F4 enriched for biological functions associated with endometrial tissue repair including response to wounding, reproductive structure development, response to oxidative stress and regulation of vasculature development.
claims.source: Unbiased GO analysis enriched for biological functions that are associated with endometrial tissue repair including response to wounding, reproductive structure development, response to oxidative stress and regulation of vasculature development.
claims.evidence: Based on gene ontology analysis of F4 cluster shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: GO analysis of F4 identified functions including epithelium migration, morphogenesis of a branching epithelium and regulation of epithelial cell migration.
claims.source: Additional functions that were identified included epithelium migration, morphogenesis of a branching epithelium and regulation of epithelial cell migration (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Based on gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Cluster F4 was the only mesenchymal cell cluster that expressed markers known to be associated with both definitive mesenchymal (Pdgfrb, Vim) and epithelial (Epcam, Krt18) cell types.
claims.source: Cluster F4 was the only mesenchymal cell cluster that expressed markers known to be associated with both definitive mesenchymal (Pdgfrb, Vim) and epithelial (Epcam, Krt18) cell types (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNAseq data showing co-expression of mesenchymal and epithelial markers in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: F4 was the only cluster that expressed genes associated with both mesenchymal/fibroblast markers and epithelial markers.
claims.source: Comparison across all mesenchymal clusters of the expression of both known canonical mesenchymal/fibroblast markers including Thy1, Cd34, Cdh11, Col1a1, Col3a1, Fbln1, Fbln2, Mfap4, and Mfap5 and epithelial markers such as Krt8, Krt19, Muc1, Muc4, Cd24a, Car2, Sdc4, Alcam, and Cdh1 revealed F4 to be the only cluster that expressed genes associated with both cell types.
claims.evidence: Based on comprehensive gene expression analysis across all clusters.

claims.claim: F4 did not express the full array of keratins and mucins associated with definitive epithelial lineages but preferentially expressed Alcam, Cd24a, Clu, Krt18, and Sdc4.
claims.source: Notably, F4 did not express the full array of keratins and mucins associated with definitive epithelial lineages but preferentially expressed Alcam, Cd24a, Clu, Krt18, and Sdc4 when compared to other mesenchymal clusters (Figure 2D; red box).
claims.evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: F4 cells may be of an intermediate phenotype and represent cells undergoing a mesenchymal to epithelial transition (MET) but not yet fully committed to a definitive epithelial lineage.
claims.source: We considered this was evidence that these cells may be of an intermediate phenotype and represent cells undergoing a mesenchymal to epithelial transition (MET) but not yet fully committed to a definitive epithelail lineage.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on the gene expression patterns observed in F4.

claims.claim: F4 expressed key transcription factors associated with MET/EMT including Cemip, Cited1, Ctnnb1, Grem1, Hmga2, Klf4, and Twist2.
claims.source: This analysis identified that F4 also expressed key transcription factors associated with MET/EMT including Cemip, Cited1, Ctnnb1, Grem1, Hmga2, Klf4, and Twist2 (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: Based on analysis of MET/EMT-associated genes from MSigDB shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Cells that expressed both GFP and EPCAM were identified in endometrial tissue undergoing active repair (24 hr) specifically in regions where the stromal surface was denuded after decidual shedding and where a new epithelial cell layer was being re-instated.
claims.source: Cells that expressed both GFP and EPCAM were identified in endometrial tissue undergoing active repair (24 hr; Figure 3A (i); white arrows) specifically in regions where (a) the stromal surface was denuded after decidual shedding and (b) a new epithelial cell layer was being re-instated.
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Some GFP+EPCAM+ cells persisted in the luminal layer at 48 hr but were not detected in 72 hr tissue.
claims.source: Some GFP + EPCAM + cells persisted in the luminal layer at 48 hr but were not detected in 72 hr tissue (Figure 3A ii, iii).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: In control/cycling endometrium expression of the GFP reporter was exclusive to the stromal compartment and epithelial cells were EPCAM+.
claims.source: Consistent with previous data in control/cycling endometrium expression of the GFP reporter was exclusive to the stromal compartment and epithelial cells were EPCAM + (yellow arrows, Figure 3A iv; Kirkwood et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 3A and citation to Kirkwood et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Flow cytometry confirmed the presence of a new population of cells that expressed both GFP and EPCAM at 24 hr with a reduction in their number at 48 hr.
claims.source: Analysis of the same tissues using flow cytometry confirmed the presence of a new population of cells that expressed both GFP and EPCAM at 24 hr with a reduction in their number at 48 hr and levels that appeared comparable to cycling/control tissues in the fully remodelled tissue (72 hr) (Figure 3B–C).
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B-C.

claims.claim: At 24 hr, GFP+EPCAM+ cells represented ~12.78% of GFP+ cells.
claims.source: Bar plot: quantification of FC data analysing the expression of EPCAM by GFP reporter positive cells in the uterus (%) - control (n=21) 0.53 ± 0.46%; 24 hr (n=30) 12.78 ± 2.49%; 48 hr (n=17) 3.71 ± 1.36%; 72 hr (n=6) 0.96 ± 0.47%; one-way ANOVA, Sidak's multiple comparisons.
claims.evidence: Quantitative flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Bioinformatic analysis combining GFP+ datasets and GFP-EPCAM+ epithelial cell data identified 16 distinct cell clusters.
claims.source: Bioinformatic analysis combining GFP + datasets (cycling/24 hr/48 hr) and GFP-EPCAM + epithelial cell data (cycling/48 hr) identified 16 distinct cell clusters (Figure 4A and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by integrated scRNAseq analysis shown in Figure 4A and C.

claims.claim: Seven of the 16 clusters had a mesenchyme phenotype: three perivascular (V, P1-2), four fibroblast (F1-4).
claims.source: Based on expression of Pdgfrb (Figure 4Bii) and canonical markers (Figure 4D) seven of these had a mesenchyme phenotype: three perivascular (V, P1-2), four fibroblast (F1-4).
claims.evidence: Based on marker gene expression shown in Figure 4B and 4D.

claims.claim: Nine of the 16 clusters expressed classical markers of epithelial cells including Epcam (E1-9).
claims.source: Nine of the clusters expressed classical markers of epithelial cells including Epcam (E1-9) (Figure 4A and B (i, ii), C).
claims.evidence: Based on marker gene expression shown in Figure 4A, B, and C.

claims.claim: The repair-specific fibroblasts (F4) formed a cluster which appeared in close proximity to both fibroblast and epithelial cell clusters but remained distinct from definitive perivascular cells.
claims.source: Notably, the previously identified repair-specific fibroblasts (F4) formed a cluster which appeared in close proximity to both fibroblast and epithelial cell clusters but remained distinct from definitive perivascular cells (V, P1, P2).
claims.evidence: Based on UMAP visualization of integrated scRNAseq data showing spatial relationships between clusters.

claims.claim: A high degree of similarity was observed between the transcriptomic signature of F4 and the definitive epithelial cell clusters E1 and E2.
claims.source: A high degree of similarity was observed between the transcriptomic signature of F4 and the definitive epithelial cell clusters E1 and E2 (Figure 4C, red box, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by heatmap analysis shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Cluster F4 uniquely expressed genes associated with both fibroblast and epithelial lineages.
claims.source: Extended analysis of canonical markers of mesenchymal (perivascular/fibroblast) and epithelial cell types confirmed that cluster F4 uniquely expressed genes associated with both fibroblast and epithelial lineages (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C(i-iv)).
claims.evidence: Supported by comprehensive marker analysis shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The repair-specific mesenchyme cluster F4 expressed genes associated with both luminal (Fxyd4, Gsto1, Plac8, Ctsl, Lgals3, Cited2) and differentiating (Ctnnb1, Krt8, Krt18, Plk2, Basp1, Ptgs2, Olfm1) epithelial cell phenotypes.
claims.source: Notably, the repair-specific mesenchyme cluster F4 also expressed genes associated with both luminal (Fxyd4, Gsto1, Plac8, Ctsl, Lgals3, Cited2) and differentiating (Ctnnb1, Krt8, Krt18, Plk2, Basp1, Ptgs2, Olfm1) epithelial cell phenotypes with no expression of genes considered definitive for glandular epithelium (Foxa2, Cxcl15).
claims.evidence: Based on gene expression analysis of epithelial subtype markers shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: F4 had no expression of genes considered definitive for glandular epithelium (Foxa2, Cxcl15).
claims.source: Notably, the repair-specific mesenchyme cluster F4 also expressed genes associated with both luminal (Fxyd4, Gsto1, Plac8, Ctsl, Lgals3, Cited2) and differentiating (Ctnnb1, Krt8, Krt18, Plk2, Basp1, Ptgs2, Olfm1) epithelial cell phenotypes with no expression of genes considered definitive for glandular epithelium (Foxa2, Cxcl15).
claims.evidence: Based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Monocle3 analysis segregated the scRNAseq data into two partitions: one that encompassed the perivascular subsets and one that contained both the fibroblast and epithelial subsets.
claims.source: Monocle3 analysis segregated the scRNAseq data into two partitions: one that encompassed the perivascular subsets; and one that contained both the fibroblast and epithelial subsets.
claims.evidence: Based on Monocle3 trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: This pattern would be consistent with genetic changes linking fibroblasts and epithelial cells but none between either fibroblasts or epithelial cells and the perivascular clusters.
claims.source: We infer that this would be consistent with a pattern of genetic changes linking fibroblasts and epithelial cells but none between either fibroblasts or epithelial cells and the perivascular clusters (Figure 5A i-ii).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the Monocle3 trajectory analysis results.

claims.claim: Monocle3 identified a root within fibroblast cluster F2 with a branch moving through the repair-specific cluster F4 into a root in the epithelial clusters on the border of E1 and E2.
claims.source: Further interrogation of the Monocle data identified a 'root' within fibroblast cluster F2 with a branch moving through the repair-specific cluster F4 into a root in the epithelial clusters on the border of E1 and E2, with subsequent branches moving into other epithelial subsets (Figure 5A iii).
claims.evidence: Based on Monocle3 trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5A iii.

claims.claim: No roots were placed within the F4 cluster (only a trajectory branch), which suggests this population does not have a terminally differentiated phenotype but represents a transitional transcriptional state.
claims.source: No roots were placed within the F4 cluster (only a trajectory branch; Figure 5A i-iii) which further suggests this population does not have a terminally differentiated phenotype, rather it represents a transitional transcriptional state.
claims.evidence: Based on interpretation of Monocle3 trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: scVelo analysis showed a transition from F2 to F4, with cells in the F4 cluster displaying a positive unspliced/spliced ratio reinforcing their potential for cellular transition towards the epithelial clusters (E1/2).
claims.source: A transition from F2 to F4 was observed, inferring the presence of pseudotemporal dynamics between the two subpopulations, with cells in the F4 cluster displaying a positive unspliced/spliced ratio reinforcing their potential for cellular transition in the direction away from F2 and towards the epithelial clusters (E1/2) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B; red asterisk).
claims.evidence: Based on RNA velocity analysis using scVelo shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B.

claims.claim: scVelo analysis showed a transition from P1 to P2.
claims.source: Similarly, a transition from P1 to P2 was observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B; blue asterisk).
claims.evidence: Based on RNA velocity analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B.

claims.claim: The transitions within epithelial sub-populations E1/2 appeared to move away from F4 and towards E1 and E2.
claims.source: Notably, the transitions within epithelial sub-populations E1/2 appeared to move away from F4 and towards E1 and E2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B; green asterisk).
claims.evidence: Based on RNA velocity analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B.

claims.claim: A cellular transition from F1/2/3 through F4 into E1/2 may exist.
claims.source: Taken together, these bioinformatic analyses suggest that a cellular transition from F1/2/3 through F4 into E1/2 may exist.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on Monocle3 and scVelo trajectory analyses.

claims.claim: In the Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mouse uterus tdTm expression was detected in cells dispersed throughout the endometrial stromal compartment, but not in cells of the myometrium or luminal/glandular epithelium.
claims.source: In the Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mouse uterus tdTm expression was detected in cells dispersed throughout the endometrial stromal compartment, but not in cells of the myometrium or luminal/glandular epithelium (Figure 5D ii).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5D ii.

claims.claim: The tdTm expression pattern in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice replicated the location of GFPdim stromal fibroblasts in the Pdgfrb-BAC-eGFP mouse uterus.
claims.source: This pattern replicated the location of GFPdim stromal fibroblasts in the Pdgfrb-BAC-eGFP mouse uterus (Figure 5D i)
claims.evidence: Based on comparison of immunohistochemistry patterns between the two mouse lines shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Co-localisation of tdTm and native protein PDGFRα was confirmed in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice.
claims.source: We confirmed co-localisation of tdTm and native protein PDGFRα (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: tdTm+ cells in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice did not express CD146.
claims.source: We also confirmed that these tdTm + cells did not express CD146 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and concluded that the tdTM transgene is specific to PDGFRα+endometrial fibroblasts.
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The tdTM transgene is specific to PDGFRα+ endometrial fibroblasts.
claims.source: We also confirmed that these tdTm + cells did not express CD146 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and concluded that the tdTM transgene is specific to PDGFRα+endometrial fibroblasts.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple validation experiments including co-localization with PDGFRα and absence of CD146.

claims.claim: In the iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mouse uterus tdTm was detected in groups of cells dispersed throughout the stromal compartment but not the myometrium or epithelium (luminal/glandular).
claims.source: In the iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mouse uterus tdTm was detected in groups of cells dispersed throughout the stromal compartment but not the myometrium or epithelium (luminal/ glandular) (Figure 5D iii).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5D iii.

claims.claim: The tdTm pattern in iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice was similar to perivascular GFPbright cells in the Pdgfrb-BAC-eGFP mouse uterus.
claims.source: This pattern was similar to perivascular GFPbright cells in the Pdgfrb-BAC-eGFP mouse uterus (Figure 5D (i); Kirkwood et al., 2021), and therefore appeared to represent perivascular cells.
claims.evidence: Based on comparison of immunohistochemistry patterns and citation to Kirkwood et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Co-localisation of tdTm reporter with native NG2 protein was confirmed in iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice.
claims.source: To confirm this we co-localised the tdTm reporter with native NG2 protein (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: tdTm+ cells in iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice express the canonical pericyte/vSMC marker CD146 but not the endothelial cell marker CD31.
claims.source: We also confirmed they express the canonical pericyte/vSMC marker CD146 but not the endothelial cell marker CD31.
claims.evidence: Based on immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry validation experiments.

claims.claim: Induced tdTm expression in the iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mouse uterus correctly targets NG2+ perivascular cells (pericytes/vSMC).
claims.source: Taken together, we concluded that induced tdTm expression in the iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mouse uterus correctly targets NG2 + perivascular cells (pericytes/vSMC).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple validation experiments including co-localization with NG2 and expression of CD146.

claims.claim: In Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice at 24 hr after progesterone withdrawal, a unique population of tdTm+EPCAM+ cells were detected in regions where the decidualised tissue had detached leaving the stromal surface denuded.
claims.source: Notably in the 24 hr tissue a unique population of tdTm + cells that co-expressed the epithelial cell marker EPCAM (tdTm + EPCAM + cells) were detected in two regions one where the decidualised tissue had detached leaving the stromal surface denuded (Figure 6A i-iii; white arrows) and the second population having a phenotype that resembled a new epithelial layer which in some cases was continuous with tdTm-EPCAM + cells (Figure 6A iv; white and yellow arrows respectively).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: In Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice at 24 hr, tdTm+EPCAM+ cells were detected having a phenotype that resembled a new epithelial layer which in some cases was continuous with tdTm-EPCAM+ cells.
claims.source: Notably in the 24 hr tissue a unique population of tdTm + cells that co-expressed the epithelial cell marker EPCAM (tdTm + EPCAM + cells) were detected in two regions one where the decidualised tissue had detached leaving the stromal surface denuded (Figure 6A i-iii; white arrows) and the second population having a phenotype that resembled a new epithelial layer which in some cases was continuous with tdTm-EPCAM + cells (Figure 6A iv; white and yellow arrows respectively).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: In other regions of Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm tissue at 24 hr, epithelial cells that did not express tdTM were present.
claims.source: In other regions epithelial cells that did not express tdTM were present (Figure 6A v; yellow arrows).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: A transient population of tdTm+CD90+EPCAM+ cells were detected at 24 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice which represented ~20% of the reporter+ population.
claims.source: A transient population of tdTm + CD90+EPCAM + cells were detected at 24 hr (red box) which represented ~20% of the reporter + population (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B-C.

claims.claim: At 24 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice, tdTm+CD90+EPCAM+ cells represented 19.76 ± 3.24% of tdTm+ cells.
claims.source: Bar plot: quantification of tdTm + CD90+EPCAM + cells at 24/48/72 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2;Rosa26-tdTm uterine tissue, calculated as a frequency of tdTm + cells: Control (n=9): 0.45 ± 0.51%; 24 hr (n=4): 19.76 ± 3.24%; 48 hr (n=9): 0.96 ± 0.64%; 72 hr (n=13): 0.48 ± 0.54%; one-way ANOVA; Tukey's multiple comparisons.
claims.evidence: Quantitative flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Whilst some tdTM+ cells continued to co-express EPCAM at 48 or 72 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice, these cells were CD90-.
claims.source: Notably whilst some of the tdTM + cells continued to co-express EPCAM at 48 or 72 hr tissue these cells were CD90- (Figure 6C iii-iv).
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: In NG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice, cells with a tdTm+CD90+ phenotype were identified in controls and at 24, 48, and 72 hr after induction of repair.
claims.source: When identical analysis methods were applied to tissue recovered from the NG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice cells with a tdTm + CD90+phenotype were identified in controls and at 24, 48, and 72 hr after induction of repair (Figure 6D)
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: In NG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice, no tdTm+EPCAM+ cells were detected nor were any tdTm+ cells present in the epithelial cells at any timepoint.
claims.source: however using sensitive flow cytometry no tdTm + EPCAM + cells were detected nor were any tdTm + cells present in the epithelial cells at any timepoint (Figure 6D–F).
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6D-F.

claims.claim: tdTm+ cells were identified in the luminal epithelium at 48 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice adjacent to tdTm- epithelial cells.
claims.source: Notably we identified tdTm + cells in the luminal epithelium at 48 hr adjacent to tdTm- epithelial cells (Figure 7A (i-iv); white and yellow arrows respectively).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: tdTm+ and tdTm- epithelial cell populations were detected in uterine tissues at 72 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice.
claims.source: These two populations of cells were also detected in uterine tissues at 72 hr (Figure 7B iv).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: tdTm expression was not identified in epithelial cell populations at the time of progesterone withdrawal (0 hr) in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice.
claims.source: Importantly, tdTm expression was not identified in epithelial cell populations at the time of progesterone withdrawal (0 hr; Figure 7B (i); yellow arrows).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Quantification of tdTm reporter protein in EPCAM+ epithelial cells revealed time dependent changes with proportions rising from ~6% at 24 hr to ~17% at 48 hr and ~15% at 72 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice.
claims.source: Quantification of tdTm reporter protein in EPCAM +epithelial cells revealed time dependent changes with proportions rising from ~6% at 24 hr to ~17% at 48 hr and ~15% at 72 hr (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry quantification shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: At 48 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice, 16.63 ± 2.24% of EPCAM+ cells expressed tdTm.
claims.source: Bar plot: quantification of FC data analysing EPCAM + cells that express tdTm in Pdgfra-creERT2;Rosa26-tdTm uterine tissues 24, 48, and 72 hr following progesterone withdrawal, calculated as a frequency of EPCAM + cells: Control (n=9): 0.75 ± 0.35%; 24 hr (n=4): 3.73 ± 1.81%; 48 h (n=9): 16.63 ± 2.24%; 72 hr (n=13): 13.26 ± 2.42%; one-way ANOVA; Tukey's multiple comparisons.
claims.evidence: Quantitative flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: At 72 hr in Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice, 13.26 ± 2.42% of EPCAM+ cells expressed tdTm.
claims.source: Bar plot: quantification of FC data analysing EPCAM + cells that express tdTm in Pdgfra-creERT2;Rosa26-tdTm uterine tissues 24, 48, and 72 hr following progesterone withdrawal, calculated as a frequency of EPCAM + cells: Control (n=9): 0.75 ± 0.35%; 24 hr (n=4): 3.73 ± 1.81%; 48 h (n=9): 16.63 ± 2.24%; 72 hr (n=13): 13.26 ± 2.42%; one-way ANOVA; Tukey's multiple comparisons.
claims.evidence: Quantitative flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: The presence of groups of tdTm+EPCAM+ adjacent to tdTm-EPCAM+ cells in the newly formed luminal epithelium at 48 hr and their persistence at 72 hr is consistent with MET by PDGFRα+ fibroblasts and retention/proliferation of existing epithelial cells both contributing to rapid repair.
claims.source: The presence of groups of tdTm + EPCAM + adjacent to tdTm-EPCAM + cells in the newly formed luminal epithelium at 48 hr and their persistence at 72 hr is consistent with MET by PDGFRα+fibroblasts and retention/proliferation of existing epithelial cells both contributing to rapid repair.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on the lineage tracing data showing both tdTm+ and tdTm- epithelial cells.

claims.claim: No tdTm+EPCAM+ cells were detected in NG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice at any timepoint.
claims.source: Importantly we never detected, an equivalent population of tdTm + EPCAM + cells in NG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice at any timepoint (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–E).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Mice with stabilisation of Ctnnb1 had smaller uteri, endometrial gland defects, and were infertile.
claims.source: Notably it has previously been reported that mice with stabilisation of Ctnnb1, a gene that plays an important role in Wnt signalling, had smaller uteri, endometrial gland defects, and were infertile (Stewart et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Stewart et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Huang et al. used a knock-in strategy with cells expressing LacZ induced by Amhr2-Cre and found labelled cells in both luminal and glandular epithelium post-partum.
claims.source: For example, Huang et al used a knock-in strategy with cells expressing LacZ induced by Amhr2-Cre: in virgin females the reporter was specific to stromal cells but post-partum they found labelled cells in both luminal and glandular epithelium.
claims.evidence: This is a description of findings from Huang et al., 2012 as discussed in the manuscript.

claims.claim: In a study using a SM22a-Cre driver, reporter gene expression (GFP) was detected in the epithelium.
claims.source: In another study using a SM22a-Cre driver, expression of which was reported to be restricted to a subset of CD34 +mesenchymal cells, reporter gene expression (GFP) was also detected in the epithelium (Yin et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Yin et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Ghosh et al. questioned whether epithelial cells expressing reporter proteins in the adult endometrium arose from MET or were induced at a time when cells had meso-epithelial characteristics.
claims.source: Specifically, Ghosh et al conducted a comprehensive examination of embryonic and adult reproductive tracts using LacZ reporter lines driven by promoters for the genes Amhr2, Sm22, Cspg4, Thy1 and Pdgfrß all of which are expressed in mesenchyme. They specifically questioned whether epithelial cells expressing reporter proteins in the adult endometrium arose from MET or were induced at a time when cells had meso-epithelial characteristics.

results.result: Single-cell RNA sequencing of PDGFRβ+ mesenchymal cells from cycling mice and at 24 and 48 hr after progesterone withdrawal identified 8 transcriptionally distinct clusters, including 3 perivascular populations (V, P1, P2) and 5 fibroblast subpopulations (F1-5). Three repair-specific clusters (P2, F4, F5) were identified that were not present in cycling tissue.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C35 are well-supported by scRNAseq data with appropriate visualization (Figure 1B-D), marker gene expression analysis (Figure 1C), and comparison to previously published cycling tissue data (Kirkwood et al., 2021). The cell isolation strategy (CD31-/CD45-/GFP+) is validated by absence of endothelial and immune markers (C32-C33).

results.result: The repair-specific pericyte cluster P2 showed high similarity to P1 and expressed genes associated with blood vessel formation and immune cell signaling characteristic of pericytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C37 are supported by differential gene expression analysis (Figure 2A) and unbiased GO analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D). The functional characterization is consistent with known pericyte biology.

results.result: Cluster F5 (48 hr specific) expressed mitochondrial genes and apoptosis markers (Casp3, Casp9, Trp53, Bax) and was identified as representing dead/apoptotic cells, leading to its exclusion from further analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C40 are supported by scRNAseq data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C), GO analysis showing DNA damage functions, and corroboration with previous cleaved caspase data (Armstrong et al., 2017). The decision to exclude this cluster from downstream analysis is justified.

results.result: The repair-specific cluster F4 (24 hr) had a unique transcriptomic signature distinct from cycling fibroblasts, expressed both mesenchymal (Pdgfrb, Vim) and epithelial (Epcam, Krt18) markers, and showed enrichment for GO terms related to tissue repair, epithelial migration, and MET/EMT transcription factors. F4 cells appear to represent an intermediate phenotype undergoing mesenchymal to epithelial transition.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C48 are strongly supported by multiple lines of evidence: differential gene expression (Figure 2A), GO analysis (Figure 2B), co-expression of mesenchymal and epithelial markers (Figure 2C-D), and expression of MET/EMT transcription factors from MSigDB (Figure 2E). The interpretation of F4 as an intermediate/transitional state is reasonable given the gene expression patterns, though this remains inferential until validated by lineage tracing.

results.result: Immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry confirmed the presence of GFP+EPCAM+ cells in Pdgfrb-BAC-eGFP mice at 24 hr after progesterone withdrawal in regions of denuded stroma and newly forming epithelium. These cells represented ~12.78% of GFP+ cells at 24 hr, decreased to ~3.71% at 48 hr, and were not detected at 72 hr.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C53 are supported by immunohistochemistry (Figure 3A) and quantitative flow cytometry data (Figure 3B-C) with appropriate statistical analysis (one-way ANOVA, n=21-30 per group). The temporal dynamics are consistent with a transient population. However, a limitation is that GFP expression depends on active Pdgfrb promoter activity, so loss of signal could reflect either cell loss or promoter inactivation.

results.result: Integration of GFP+ mesenchymal and GFP-EPCAM+ epithelial scRNAseq datasets identified 16 distinct clusters (7 mesenchymal, 9 epithelial). The repair-specific F4 cluster formed a distinct population in close proximity to both fibroblast and epithelial clusters, showed high transcriptomic similarity to epithelial clusters E1 and E2, and uniquely expressed genes from both fibroblast and epithelial lineages including luminal and differentiating epithelial markers but not glandular markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C61 are well-supported by integrated scRNAseq analysis with appropriate visualization (Figure 4A-C), marker expression analysis (Figure 4D), and epithelial subtype characterization (Figure 4E). The spatial positioning of F4 between fibroblast and epithelial clusters on UMAP is consistent with an intermediate state. Doublet analysis was performed to confirm F4 is not an artifact (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).

results.result: In silico trajectory analysis using Monocle3 and scVelo identified a putative differentiation trajectory from fibroblast cluster F2 through the repair-specific F4 cluster to epithelial clusters E1/E2. F4 had no trajectory roots (only a branch), suggesting it represents a transitional rather than terminally differentiated state. RNA velocity analysis showed positive unspliced/spliced ratios in F4 cells consistent with transition toward epithelial clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C69 are supported by appropriate computational trajectory analyses (Monocle3 in Figure 5A, scVelo in Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The methods are standard for inferring cell state transitions from scRNAseq data. However, these are computational predictions that require experimental validation through lineage tracing, which is provided in subsequent experiments. The interpretation that F4 represents a transitional state is reasonable but remains inferential from the trajectory analysis alone.

results.result: In Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice, tdTm expression was detected throughout the endometrial stromal compartment but not in myometrium or epithelium, replicating the pattern of GFPdim stromal fibroblasts in Pdgfrb-BAC-eGFP mice. Co-localization with native PDGFRα and absence of CD146 expression confirmed the tdTM transgene specifically targets PDGFRα+ endometrial fibroblasts.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C74 are well-supported by immunohistochemistry (Figure 5D-E), co-localization studies, and flow cytometry validation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2). The characterization includes appropriate positive (PDGFRα) and negative (CD146, CD31) markers. The 4-week tamoxifen washout period was validated to ensure tissue responsiveness was restored.

results.result: In iNG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice, tdTm was detected in groups of cells throughout the stromal compartment but not in myometrium or epithelium, with a pattern similar to perivascular GFPbright cells in Pdgfrb-BAC-eGFP mice. Co-localization with native NG2 and expression of CD146 but not CD31 confirmed the transgene correctly targets NG2+ perivascular cells (pericytes/vSMC).
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C79 are well-supported by immunohistochemistry (Figure 5D, F), co-localization studies, and marker validation. The characterization appropriately distinguishes perivascular cells from fibroblasts and endothelial cells using established markers.

results.result: In Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice at 24 hr after progesterone withdrawal, a unique population of tdTm+EPCAM+ cells was detected in regions of denuded stroma and newly forming epithelium, representing 19.76 ± 3.24% of tdTm+ cells. These cells were also CD90+ at 24 hr but became CD90- at 48 and 72 hr while some continued to express EPCAM.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C85 are strongly supported by immunohistochemistry (Figure 6A) and quantitative flow cytometry (Figure 6B-C) with appropriate statistical analysis (one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparisons, n=4-13 per group). The temporal dynamics and marker expression patterns are consistent with cells undergoing MET. The loss of CD90 while retaining EPCAM at later timepoints suggests progressive epithelialization.

results.result: In NG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice, tdTm+CD90+ cells were identified at all timepoints, but no tdTm+EPCAM+ cells were detected at any timepoint by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C87 are supported by flow cytometry (Figure 6D-E) and immunohistochemistry (Figure 6F) data. This negative control is critical for demonstrating that MET occurs specifically in PDGFRα+ fibroblasts and not in NG2+ perivascular cells, strengthening the specificity of the findings.

results.result: In Pdgfra-creERT2/Rosa26-tdTm mice, tdTm+ cells were identified in the luminal epithelium at 48 hr adjacent to tdTm- epithelial cells and persisted at 72 hr. tdTm was not detected in epithelium at 0 hr (progesterone withdrawal). Quantification showed tdTm expression in EPCAM+ cells rose from ~3.73% at 24 hr to 16.63 ± 2.24% at 48 hr and 13.26 ± 2.42% at 72 hr, consistent with MET by PDGFRα+ fibroblasts and retention/proliferation of existing epithelial cells both contributing to repair.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C94 are strongly supported by immunohistochemistry (Figure 7A-B, D) and quantitative flow cytometry (Figure 7C) with appropriate statistical analysis (one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparisons, n=4-13 per group). The absence of tdTm in epithelium at 0 hr (C90) is critical for ruling out pre-existing labeling. The persistence of tdTm+ epithelial cells at 48 and 72 hr demonstrates long-term incorporation. The interpretation that both MET and existing epithelial cell proliferation contribute to repair (C94) is reasonable given the presence of both tdTm+ and tdTm- epithelial cells.

results.result: No tdTm+EPCAM+ cells were detected in NG2-creER/Rosa26-tdTm mice at any timepoint.
results.evaluation: Claim C95 is supported by immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry data (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-E). This negative control confirms that perivascular cells do not undergo MET and contribute to the epithelium, providing specificity for the fibroblast-to-epithelium transition.

results.result: Stromal fibroblasts (PDGFRα+) can undergo mesenchyme to epithelial transformation and become incorporated into the re-epithelialized luminal surface during endometrial repair. The cell type involved in MET is PDGFRα+ stromal cells and not NG2+ pericytes. MET contributes to rapid scar-free healing of the endometrial luminal epithelium in response to menstruation.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C110, and C111 represent the main conclusions of the study and are strongly supported by the convergence of multiple lines of evidence: (1) scRNAseq identification of F4 cluster with intermediate mesenchymal-epithelial phenotype, (2) trajectory analysis suggesting fibroblast-to-epithelial transition, (3) lineage tracing in Pdgfra-creERT2 mice showing tdTm+ cells in epithelium, (4) negative results in NG2-creER mice ruling out pericyte contribution, and (5) temporal dynamics consistent with MET during the repair window. The use of inducible Cre systems in adult mice addresses previous criticisms about developmental labeling.

results.result: The mouse model used recapitulates key features of human menstruation including vascular breakdown, hypoxia, apoptosis, matrix metalloproteinase expression, and immune cell influx. Restoration of an intact luminal epithelial layer occurs within two days, with evidence for epithelial cell migration and proliferation but no significant basal gland proliferation.
results.evaluation: Claims C23-C25 are supported by multiple citations to previous validation studies (Armstrong et al., 2017; Maybin et al., 2018; Cousins et al., 2014, 2016a, 2016b). The model has been extensively characterized and is appropriate for studying endometrial repair mechanisms.

results.result: Previous work identified stromal cells co-expressing vimentin and cytokeratin in areas denuded of epithelium, suggesting MET. This is the first study to use inducible-Cre lineage tracing in adult mice to explore MET in a menstruation model.
results.evaluation: Claim C27 is supported by citation to Cousins et al., 2014. Claim C28 regarding methodological novelty appears accurate based on the literature review provided in the manuscript, though comprehensive verification of this claim would require extensive literature search. The use of inducible Cre systems in adult mice is a significant methodological advance over constitutive systems.

results.result: Comparison with published human scRNAseq data (Wu et al., 2022) identified that Sfrp4 expression was highest in mouse F2 and F4 populations, and two factors secreted by SFRP4 cells (PENK, GLIPR1) were higher in F4 than other clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C108 are supported by comparison of the current study's scRNAseq data with published data from Wu et al., 2022. This cross-species comparison suggests potential conservation of repair mechanisms, though further validation in human menstrual tissue would be needed to confirm the presence of an F4-equivalent population.

results.result: The human endometrium undergoes repetitive cycles of tissue wounding with piecemeal shedding and rapid scar-free restoration. Menstruation is triggered by progesterone withdrawal and involves inflammatory changes, prostaglandin production, vasoconstriction, hypoxia, and HIF1α stabilization.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C7-C11 provide background context and are supported by appropriate citations to established literature (Garry et al., 2009; Ludwig and Spornitz, 1991; Greenhalgh et al., 2015; Maybin and Critchley, 2011; Evans and Salamonsen, 2012; Critchley et al., 2006b). These represent well-established knowledge in the field.

results.result: Previous studies have proposed multiple mechanisms for endometrial repair including stem/progenitor cells (PDGFRB+/CD146+/SUSD2+ cells with perivascular location), epithelial proliferation from surface epithelium and basal glands, and MET of stromal cells. Historical observations documented rapid re-epithelialization (~48 hr) with piecemeal shedding and repair occurring synchronously.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C22 and C26 provide literature review context and are supported by appropriate citations (Gargett et al., 2016; Ludwig and Spornitz, 1991; Ferenczy, 1976a, 1976b; Garry et al., 2009; Armstrong et al., 2017; Baggish et al., 1967; Kaitu'u-Lino et al., 2010, 2012). The authors appropriately acknowledge competing hypotheses and previous observations.

results.result: Previous lineage tracing studies using constitutive Cre systems reported epithelial labeling that was attributed to either MET or developmental activation of mesenchymal promoters. Ghosh et al. (2020) challenged MET interpretations, attributing epithelial reporter expression to embryonic activation. The half-life of eGFP protein in vivo was reported to be ~15 hr in cancer studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C101 provide important context for interpreting the current study's findings and are supported by appropriate citations (Stewart et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2012; Yin et al., 2019; Ghosh et al., 2020; Zhao et al., 1999; Danhier et al., 2015). The authors appropriately address previous criticisms and explain how their inducible system in adult mice overcomes limitations of prior studies.

results.result: Comparison with published human endometrial scRNAseq studies showed limited direct correspondence to the mouse F4 cluster. Studies by Queckbörner et al. (2021) identified perivascular and fibroblast populations but no menstrual phase tissue. Cao et al. (2021) noted that cell culture influenced transcriptomes. Wu et al. (2022) identified SFRP4+ stromal cells distinct from SUSD2+ perivascular progenitors.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C106 and C109 provide appropriate discussion of how the current findings relate to published human scRNAseq studies. The authors appropriately acknowledge limitations in making cross-species and cross-study comparisons, particularly regarding differences in tissue processing (fresh vs. cultured), cycle phase, and technical approaches.
